You are an expert in TypeScript, Angular, and scalable web application development. You write functional, maintainable, performant, and accessible code following Angular and TypeScript best practices.

## TypeScript Best Practices

- Use strict type checking
- Prefer type inference when the type is obvious
- Avoid the `any` type; use `unknown` when type is uncertain

## Angular Best Practices

- Always use angular schematics for new files (ng generate ...) unless there is no generator
  - Do not change options - schematic will use angular.json defaults
  - For pages use `ng g c ... --type=page`
  - For models use `ng g interface ...`
  - For data sources and services use `ng g s ...`

- Always use standalone components over NgModules
- Must NOT set `standalone: true` inside Angular decorators. It's the default in Angular v20+.
- Do NOT set `changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush` explicitly. `OnPush` is the default in Angular v22+.
- Use signals for state management
- Implement lazy loading for feature routes
- Do NOT use the `@HostBinding` and `@HostListener` decorators. Put host bindings inside the `host` object of the `@Component` or `@Directive` decorator instead
- Use `NgOptimizedImage` for all static images.
  - `NgOptimizedImage` does not work for inline base64 images.

## Accessibility Requirements

- It MUST pass all AXE checks.
- It MUST follow all WCAG AA minimums, including focus management, color contrast, and ARIA attributes.

## Components

- Keep components small and focused on a single responsibility
- Use `input()` and `output()` functions instead of decorators
- Use `model()` for two-way bound properties with `[(prop)]` syntax instead of pairing `input()` with `output()`
- Use `computed()` for derived state
- Use `linkedSignal()` for state derived from multiple reactive sources that must stay synchronized
- Prefer inline templates for small components
- Prefer Signal Forms (`@angular/forms/signals`) for new forms. They are stable in Angul

import { Component, computed, input, signal } from '@angular/core';

import { single } from 'rxjs';

export const DealStageConfig: Record<DealStage, { label: string; class: string }> = {
  new: { label: 'New', class: 'bg-amber-400' },
  proposal: { label: 'Proposal', class: 'bg-blue-400' },
  negotiation: { label: 'Negotiation', class: 'bg-red-400' },
  'closed-lost': { label: 'Closed (Lost)', class: 'bg-gray-400' },
  'closed-won': { label: 'Closed (Won)', class: 'bg-green-500' },
} as const;

@Component({
  imports: [],
  selector: 'app-deal-stage-badge',
  styles: `
    :host {
      display: block;
    }
  `,
  template: ` <span class="rounded px-3 py-1 text-label-md " [class]="stageConfig().class">
    {{ stageConfig().label }}
  </span>`,
})
export class DealStageBadge {
  public readonly stage = input.required<DealStage>();

  // TODO: Fetch config from API
  protected readonly dynamicConfig = signal(DealStageConfig);

  protected readonly stageConfig = computed(() => {
    const configs = this.dynamicConfig();
    
    // if(!configs) // Not loaded yet!

    return configs[this.stage()];
  });
}

## Plan: Extend DealEditor form with Deal fields

Add description, stage, contactName, public to the reactive form in `DealEditor`, populate all fields from the `deal()` input, lay them out in `app-info-grid`. Move `DealStageConfig` to `model/` as a separate file. Only `title` stays required.

Steps
1. Create `src/app/features/deals/model/deal-stage-config.ts` with `DealStageConfig` moved from deal-stage-badge.ts, plus an ordered options array. No other importers of `DealStageConfig` exist.
2. Update `src/app/features/deals/ui/deal-stage-badge/deal-stage-badge.ts` to import `DealStageConfig` from the model file and remove the local definition. *depends on 1*
3. In `deal-editor.ts`, extend `form` with `description`, `stage` (typed `DealStage`, default `'new'`), `contactName`, `public`. Keep `title` (required + censor) and `value`. Use `this.bob.control<T>()` for typed non-nullable controls. *depends on 1*
4. Populate the form from the input: `effect(() => this.form.reset(this.deal()))` in the constructor. The existing unused `effect` import is reused. Input values are not available in field initializers.
5. Template: wrap fields in `<app-info-grid>` (`InfoGrid` comes from `@shared/ui`, which already exports `SharedUI`). Order: title (full row), stage / value / contactName (3 columns), description textarea (full row), public checkbox. Add `sm:col-span-3` to full-width items.
6. Stage `mat-select` iterates the options array with `@for`, `mat-option` label from `DealStageConfig[stage].label`. Expose config/options as `protected readonly` fields.
7. Keep the `<pre>{{ form.value | json }}</pre>` debug block and the Save/Cancel buttons unchanged.

Relevant files
- `src/app/features/deals/ui/deal-editor/deal-editor.ts` — main changes (form, effect, template, imports `SharedForms, SharedUI`).
- `src/app/features/deals/ui/deal-stage-badge/deal-stage-badge.ts` — import config instead of defining it.
- `src/app/features/deals/model/deal-stage-config.ts` — new file (config extracted).
- `src/app/features/deals/model/deal.ts` — `DealStage` and `Deal` unchanged.
- `src/app/features/deals/pages/deals-search/deals-search.page.ts` — no change; consumes `(save)` and `(cancel)`.
- `src/app/shared/index.ts` — `SharedForms`, `SharedUI` reused, no change.

Verification
1. `npx ng build` compiles without template or type errors.
2. Open deals search, click edit: all fields show values from the selected deal.
3. Change each field, click Save: the emitted draft contains the new values for all six fields.
4. Cancel closes the editor without emitting `save`.
5. Stage dropdown shows five options with the same labels as the badge.
6. Public checkbox toggles and reflects the saved value. Title required error still shows when empty.
7. Check labels for each field in the browser accessibility tree (AXE-style check).

Decisions
- Keep Reactive forms, do not migrate to Signal Forms (out of scope, matches existing code).
- No new validators beyond existing `title`. `value` `required` error message exists in the template but there is no validator, so it never fires (left unchanged).
- Config moved as-is (labels and Tailwind classes together) because that is what was requested.

Further considerations
1. `DealStageConfig` contains Tailwind `class` strings, which are presentation concerns in `model/`. Option A: move as-is (matches request). Option B: keep labels in model, move classes into the badge component.
2. `effect` with `form.reset` re-runs whenever `deal` changes while the editor stays mounted. Option A: effect (keeps form in sync). Option B: `ngOnInit` patch (runs once). Recommend A.

import { Component, computed, input, signal } from '@angular/core';

export const DealStageConfig: Record<DealStage, { label: string; class: string }> = {
  new: { label: 'New', class: 'bg-amber-400' },
  proposal: { label: 'Proposal', class: 'bg-blue-400' },
  negotiation: { label: 'Negotiation', class: 'bg-red-400' },
  'closed-lost': { label: 'Closed (Lost)', class: 'bg-gray-400' },
  'closed-won': { label: 'Closed (Won)', class: 'bg-green-500' },
} as const;

@Component({
  imports: [],
  selector: 'app-deal-stage-badge',
  styles: `
    :host {
      display: block;
    }
  `,
  template: ` <span class="rounded px-3 py-1 text-label-md " [class]="stageConfig().class">
    {{ stageConfig().label }}
  </span>`,
})
export class DealStageBadge {
  public readonly stage = input.required<DealStage>();

  // TODO: Fetch config from API
  protected readonly dynamicConfig = signal(DealStageConfig);

  protected readonly stageConfig = computed(() => {
    const configs = this.dynamicConfig();
    
    // if(!configs) // Not loaded yet!

    return configs[this.stage()];
  });
}
